stars.name: Sirius
stars.fact: The brightest star in the whole night sky, in the Big Dog.

stars.name: Canopus
stars.fact: The second-brightest star we see — a giant, glowing far away.

stars.name: Rigil Kentaurus
stars.fact: Our closest star neighbor after the Sun — it's really three stars together!

stars.name: Arcturus
stars.fact: A giant orange star, one of the brightest in the whole sky.

stars.name: Vega
stars.fact: A bright blue-white star — long ago it was even the North Star!

stars.name: Capella
stars.fact: Looks like one star, but it's really four stars close together.

stars.name: Rigel
stars.fact: A huge blue star lighting up the bottom of Orion the Hunter.

stars.name: Procyon
stars.fact: A bright nearby star that leads the Little Dog across the sky.

stars.name: Betelgeuse
stars.fact: A giant red star so big it could swallow Mars' whole orbit.

stars.name: Achernar
stars.fact: Spins so fast it's squashed flat, like a beach ball.

stars.name: Hadar
stars.fact: A hot, blazing blue giant star.

stars.name: Altair
stars.fact: Spins around super fast — once every few hours!

stars.name: Acrux
stars.fact: The top star of the tiny Southern Cross.

stars.name: Aldebaran
stars.fact: A giant orange star that looks like the Bull's fiery eye.

stars.name: Antares
stars.fact: A huge red star — the fiery heart of the Scorpion.

stars.name: Spica
stars.fact: Not one star but two, circling so close they almost touch.

stars.name: Pollux
stars.fact: The brighter of the two twin stars in Gemini.

stars.name: Fomalhaut
stars.fact: Has real rings of dust and baby planets circling around it.

stars.name: Deneb
stars.fact: One of the farthest bright stars we can see — and incredibly powerful.

stars.name: Mimosa
stars.fact: A hot blue giant star marking the Southern Cross.

stars.name: Regulus
stars.fact: The bright heart of Leo the Lion, spinning so fast it's squished.

stars.name: Adhara
stars.fact: A super hot blue star trotting along with the Big Dog.

stars.name: Polaris
stars.fact: The North Star — it barely moves all night, so sailors use it to find their way.

cons.name: The Big Dipper
cons.fact: It looks like a big spoon in the sky! People use it to find the North Star.

cons.name: Orion the Hunter
cons.fact: Orion has three stars in a row — that's his belt!

cons.name: Cassiopeia
cons.fact: It's shaped like a big letter W — a queen's crown in the sky.

cons.name: The Southern Cross
cons.fact: Sailors and pilots use this tiny cross to find south!

cons.name: Scorpius the Scorpion
cons.fact: Its curly tail has a bright red star called Antares.

cons.name: Leo the Lion
cons.fact: Leo the Lion has a bright heart-star called Regulus.

cons.name: Cygnus the Swan
cons.fact: A swan flying along the Milky Way, with its tail star Deneb.

cons.name: Taurus the Bull
cons.fact: Its bright orange eye is a star called Aldebaran.

cons.name: Gemini the Twins
cons.fact: Two bright stars side by side — Castor and Pollux, the twins.

cons.name: The Summer Triangle
cons.fact: Three super-bright stars from three different constellations, making one big triangle.

cons.name: The Little Dipper
cons.fact: A tiny spoon with the North Star, Polaris, right at the end of its handle!

cons.name: Pegasus the Flying Horse
cons.fact: A giant square in the sky — the body of a flying horse!

cons.name: Andromeda the Princess
cons.fact: A princess in the stars, connected to the flying horse Pegasus.

cons.name: Perseus the Hero
cons.fact: A hero holding a special star that blinks — that's Algol, the Demon Star!

cons.name: Auriga the Charioteer
cons.fact: The Charioteer, holding his bright goat-star, Capella.

cons.name: Boötes the Herdsman
cons.fact: The Herdsman, with the bright orange giant star Arcturus glowing below.

cons.name: Lyra the Harp
cons.fact: A tiny harp with the bright blue star Vega.

cons.name: Aquila the Eagle
cons.fact: An eagle soaring along the Milky Way, with the bright star Altair.

cons.name: The Little Dog
cons.fact: The Little Dog, trotting along with just two bright stars.

cons.name: Centaurus
cons.fact: A half-horse, half-person with two of the brightest stars in the whole sky.

cons.name: Draco the Dragon
cons.fact: A long dragon that winds all the way around the North Star.

cons.name: Corvus the Crow
cons.fact: A crow, shaped like a little kite in the sky.

cons.name: Sagittarius the Archer
cons.fact: An archer — its brightest stars make the shape of a teapot!

cons.name: The Big Dog
cons.fact: The Big Dog, led by Sirius — the very brightest star in the whole night sky!

cons.name: Aries the Ram
cons.fact: The Ram — just a simple curved line of stars.

cons.name: Cetus the Sea Monster
cons.fact: A big sea monster from an old story about a princess and a hero.
